# Answer: generator-shortcuts

Task `2692a3e47a66`, original family ARC training:22208ba4, assignment
`review-cc6df0b7bf591ff4`. Final generator SHA-256:
`ff79193bed2cc537c82a56abd6235304e2f2fb791eda67050b68bb84b048f328`.
Canonical normalized rule hash: `f5a9e05539e5` (unchanged).

## Strongest retained rival

The strongest concrete rival found is the generator's actual declared
`move_only_modal_object_color`: count disconnected foreground objects by color,
choose only the color with the largest object count (breaking ties toward the
lower numeric color), and move that color's objects inward by their own sizes.
Leave every other color unchanged. The intended rule moves **every** color that
occurs in at least two disconnected objects.

This rival fits all four canonical training demonstrations and the one retained
canonical test pair. That is measured in
`checks/canonical-review-final/report.json`, using the public `canonical_pairs`
and `load_selected_generator` helpers and the actual declared rival callable.
The other unique declared rival, `move_repeated_blocks_by_one_global_size`, also
fits all five pairs. Repeated names in `CANONICAL_SHORTCUTS`,
`LESSON_COMPETITORS`, and the semantic declarations are aliases, not six
independent rivals. The modal-color rival is the strongest observed teaching
shortcut because it also survives some complete rotated lessons and then gives
a different query answer.

## Exact generated counterexample

The following supported call, with no overrides, emits the witness:

```python
generator.generate(71, 3, difficulty="medium")
```

Its grid is **19 rows by 20 columns**. Use zero-based coordinates. Every cell is
7 except the following disjoint rectangles; endpoints are inclusive:

| Color | Rows | Columns |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 9 | 0 | 0 |
| 9 | 18 | 0 |
| 8 | 0–3 | 16–19 |
| 8 | 15–18 | 16–19 |

This specifies every cell exactly. A literal grid is retained in
`checks/canonical-review-final/rotation-witness-input.json` and the task's
`counterexamples/review-cc6df0b7bf591ff4/rotation-witness-input.json`.
Its input SHA-256 is
`b32bdb303cdbcce648142fbbd5e2f78856c5bc511bc318b7f5d4f56133a1771e`.
It passes the selected generator's validator with `self_check=[]`.

The intended output is again 19×20 and all 7 except:

| Color | Rows | Columns |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 9 | 1 | 1 |
| 9 | 17 | 1 |
| 8 | 4–7 | 12–15 |
| 8 | 11–14 | 12–15 |

There are two objects of each color. Both colors therefore move under the
intended rule. The rival resolves the 2:2 tie in favor of color 8, moves the two
side-4 blocks correctly, but leaves the two color-9 cells in their corners.
The two outputs differ at exactly four cells: `(0,0)`, `(1,1)`, `(17,1)`, and
`(18,0)`.

## How the output was checked

The saved input was passed to the public canonical Racket application, together
with the independent legal-overlap witness:

```text
cwd: packet_root
/tmp/arc_review_121953_mount/WORK/.venv/bin/python review.py run /tmp/arc_review_121953_mount/WORK/.venv/bin/python -m arcpuzzles apply 2692a3e47a66 --input ../checks/main-witnesses/inputs.json --out ../checks/main-witnesses/racket.json
```

That actual command exited **0** and returned **2/2 valid outputs**. The witness
output exactly matches the task's intended Python mirror; the comparison
command also exited 0. The exact Racket output SHA-256 is
`4b005ce9ff127cde9e266fd42f25cefb472ba1dffb0ee68bb23741b992931612`.
The executed callable SHA-256 is
`6f2be4d6bc0015577dbfe3ff8aa674e6568d5f56d342c218a3eb685ce5d70646`.
The callable hash includes the public execution wrapper; the raw canonical
registration hash is separately recorded and should not be equated with it.

Evidence: `checks/main-witnesses/command.json`, `racket.json`, `comparison.json`,
and `verify-command.json`. The self-contained task counterexample includes
`canonical-racket-witnesses.json`, `racket-comparison.json`, and `manifest.json`.
No reference program was changed to obtain agreement.

## Does the returned generator teach this distinction?

**Yes, under its designated ordered assembly.** This witness is an ordinary
scheduled `two_pairs_mixed` draw. Four consecutive demonstrations cover the four
profiles before the next draw becomes the query. The seed-71, medium,
start-zero production lesson contains indices `[0,1,2,3]` as demonstrations, so
index 3 refutes the modal-color shortcut before index 4 is asked as the query.
The returned repair preserves every grid in 108 legal pre/post comparison calls;
it does not add a new restriction or silently change the witness distribution.

**A particular reshuffle remains ambiguous.** Use the same seed and band, but
make indices `[0,1,2,4]` demonstrations and index `3` the query. The intended
rule and this rival fit all four demonstrations, then disagree on the exact
query above. The complete lesson and rival outputs are in
`checks/canonical-review-final/rotation-witness.json`. This is a demonstrated
teaching limitation despite correct Racket labels.

The final public census checks 100 production lessons per band: **300/300
ordered lessons distinguish the declared rivals**, while **226/1,500
single-query placements remain ambiguous** under the diagnostic rotation policy.
These are production-sampler lessons, with accepted indices saved in the full
reports; they are not 1,500 unique independent input draws. The independent
seed-71 cyclic-start probe checks all four starts in each band: **12/12 ordered
lessons pass**, with **9/60 ambiguous rotations**. Preserve the ordered policy;
a downstream policy allowing arbitrary query placement needs another two-pair
witness or an explicit resampling gate. This finite rival set does not establish
identifiability against every possible rule.

## Separate parameter-prototype scope

The proposed `(min_repeat, step_blocks)` prototype passes its 49 holdout checks
against the six declared parameter settings. A separate check of the saved
default episode (seed 20261019, episode 0, settings `(2,1)`) finds that holding
out its sole `[2,2]` pair at index 5 lets the same canonical rival survive the
other six examples and disagree in ten cells. Its designated query is index 6,
and its exported six demonstrations refute both canonical rivals. See
`checks/parametric/canonical-rival-scope/summary.json` and `details.json`.
The parameter-setting result is not a broader arbitrary-rotation guarantee.
